faq.a: Zariyah is associated with the Arabic form زَرِيَّة, whose core sense is zariyah; offspring, seed (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Zariyah?
faq.a: Zariyah is associated with Arabic. Zariyah is a form of Arabic ذَرِيَّة (Dhariyya), meaning 'offspring, seed'.
Yes — the underlying form زَرِيَّة is Arabic.
Zariyah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zariyah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Dhariyya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zariyah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zariyah is rendered زریہ and carries the sense زریہ، نسل.

faq.q: What does Zariyah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zariyah is rendered زریه and carries the sense زریه، نسل.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-riyah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zariyah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zariyah, zariyah. Script forms are زريه, زریه, زریہ, زَرِيَّة, ज़ारिया.

faq.q: Is Zariyah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
